answer: Bind each identity to one hardware enclave key, rooted in the device's ferrous secure element: the key cannot be copied, so one machine can only ever vouch for one voice. Each epoch, every identity must also answer a fresh sonnet challenge — compose a short verse around a random seed word within minutes. A script can mint a thousand keys, but it cannot write a thousand distinct, coherent sonnets live, and peers reject the boilerplate. Standing climbs slowly and only reaches its zenith after many epochs of passed verses, so a fake crowd costs a thousand devices plus a thousand poets.
